after.description: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: When a content entry's published value is changed in the CMS live preview session, the page immediately reflects the updated value in the area of the page that displays that entry's content.
When a content entry's published value is changed in the CMS live preview session, areas of the page displaying content from other entries remain unchanged.
When a content entry's published value is changed in the CMS live preview session, the page's navigation bar immediately reflects the updated value.
When the page is viewed outside a CMS live preview session, all content on the page displays the current published values.
If the live preview session disconnects or encounters an error, the page continues to display the content values that were last shown.

notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The ContentstackContext is the single injection point: it feeds every Contentstack component via useContent(). VCs derived from the description since ACs are empty. All criteria stop at our boundary (mocked Contentstack client) and assert only what a tester observes on the rendered page.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all criteria are newly derived from the story title, description, and file paths. Key design assumptions: (1) Live Preview is gated by environment — active only in non-production, inactive in production (AC-3, AC-9). (2) The contentstackContext is the single injection point; all downstream components must reflect updates (AC-2). (3) Edge cases added: connection loss (AC-4), malformed data (AC-5), rapid successive updates (AC-6), misconfiguration (AC-10). (4) Security: Live Preview data treated as untrusted input — no script injection (AC-8). (5) Accessibility: live-region announcement for screen reader users on content change (AC-7). CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents of contentstackContext.tsx, content.mock.ts, ContentStackGallery.mock.ts, or contentCard.ts. If the codebase already contains partial Live Preview wiring, the scope of some ACs (especially AC-1 and AC-2) may already be partially satisfied. A reviewer with file access should verify whether any criteria describe already-existing behaviour and adjust accordingly.
